title: Optimized protocol for the identification of lipid droplet proteomes using proximity labeling proteomics in cultured human cells
protocol: Incubate cells with 200 μM oleate complexed with 0.1% BSA for 24 h to increase LD abundance prior to harvesting.
Add biotin phenol to growth medium at a final concentration of 500 μM and mix gently.
Incubate cells with biotin phenol for 30 min at 37°C.
Add H2O2 from 100× stock (1 mM final concentration) to the medium for 1 min to induce biotinylation.
Aspirate medium and immediately wash three times with 5 mL quenching buffer to stop the reaction.
Wash once with 5 mL PBS to remove any residual quenching buffer.
Keep samples on ice throughout all steps of the fractionation.
Harvest cells in 3 mL PBS using a cell scraper and transfer to a chilled 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge at 500 × g for 10 min at 4°C to pellet cells, then discard supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellet in 3 mL HLM buffer containing 1× protease inhibitor and incubate on ice for 10 min.
Homogenize cells by applying 80× strokes using a tight-fitting dounce.
Transfer the homogenate to a 15 mL conical tube and centrifuge at 1000 × g for 10 min at 4°C to pellet nuclei and any unbroken cells.
Transfer the post-nuclear supernatant to a 13.2 mL ultracentrifuge tube, noting the approximate volume transferred (should be ~2–3 mL).
Dilute the post-nuclear supernatant 1:3 with 60% sucrose HLM buffer (resulting in 20% sucrose final concentration).
Pipette up-and-down several times to ensure complete mixing.
Carefully layer 5 mL of 5% sucrose HLM buffer on top, being careful not to disturb the underlying layers.
Layer an additional ~4.5 mL HLM buffer on top, leaving approximately 0.5 cm of space at the top of the tube.
Centrifuge at 28,000 × g in an SW-41TI rotor in an ultracentrifuge for 30 minutes at 4°C to pellet heavy organelles and float lipid droplets (LDs).
Handle the ultracentrifuge tubes with care after centrifugation to avoid mixing between separated layers.
Use a tube slicer to isolate the top 1 mL LD-enriched buoyant fraction.
Push the blade through the tube underneath the LD-enriched buoyant fraction.
Pipette up-and-down several times to mix the isolated fraction thoroughly.
Transfer the mixed fraction to a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Use an additional 200 μL of HLM buffer to wash the inner portion of the cut tube and tube slicer that contained the buoyant fraction.
Pipette up-and-down, paying special attention to the sides and corners.
Combine the washed buffer with the rest of the collected buoyant fraction.
Collect the remaining fractions by pipetting 1 ml at a time from the top using a micropipette.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 ml of HLM buffer.
Remove 100 μl from each fraction for western blot analysis.
Add 11.1 μL of 10% SDS to the removed sample (final concentration: 1%).
Mix the remaining portion of each fraction with 100 μL of 10% SDS (final concentration: 1%) for mass spectrometry analysis.
Sonicate all fractions once for 30 sec at 15% amplitude using a tip sonicator.
Incubate the LD fractions at 37°C for 1 hour to solubilize them.
Perform additional rounds of sonication every 20–30 min during incubation.
Separate 25 μL of each fraction by SDS-PAGE and western blotting.
Use antibodies against organelle markers such as GAPDH, PLIN2, and UBXD8 to assess the purity of each fraction.
Wash Agarose Monomeric Avidin beads twice with PBST and once with HLM buffer.
Centrifuge beads at 1000 × g for 1 min after each wash, discard supernatant.
Resuspend washed beads in 500 μL of HLM buffer.
Add resuspended beads to the diluted buoyant fraction.
Incubate mixture at room temperature on an end-over-end rotator for 4 hours.
Pellet beads by centrifugation at 1000 × g for 1 min, save flow-through for analysis if desired.
Wash beads five times with PBST and three times with PBS.
Elute biotinylated proteins from the beads using elution buffer containing 2% SDS and 3 mM biotin.
Pipette up-and-down several times to decrease shearing of the beads.
Rotate end-over-end for 15 minutes at room temperature, then heat at 95°C for 15 minutes.
Pellet beads by centrifugation at 1000 × g for 1 min and transfer eluant to a new microcentrifuge tube.
Concentrate the eluant in a centrifugal vacuum concentrator on medium heat until approximately 50 μL is remaining.
Mix the eluant with 5× Laemmli buffer.
Heat the mixture at 65°C for 5 minutes immediately prior to loading onto a polyacrylamide gel.
Load half of each sample onto neighboring lanes of the gel.
Separate proteins by SDS-PAGE until the dye front is approximately halfway down the gel.
Wash the gel three times with ddH2O for 5 minutes using an orbital shaker for constant agitation.
Add enough gel-fixing buffer containing 50% ethanol and 10% acetic acid to cover the gel.
Incubate at room temperature (RT) for 1 hour with gentle shaking.
Remove the gel-fixing buffer.
Add a gel-washing buffer containing 50% methanol and 10% acetic acid.
Incubate at RT for 30 minutes with gentle shaking.
Discard the gel-washing buffer.
Wash the gel three times with ddH2O.
Add enough Gel Code Blue G-250 stain to fully cover the gel.
Incubate at RT overnight with gentle shaking.
Wash gel with ddH2O for 4 hours at room temperature with gentle shaking, replacing ddH2O every 45 minutes to remove stain background.
Excise proteins from surrounding gel using a razor blade.
Cut excised pieces into smaller fragments to increase surface area and transfer to a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Overlay the gel pieces with 500 μL of solution containing 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate in 50% acetonitrile.
Incubate at room temperature for 40 minutes while briefly vortexing every 5-10 minutes.
Remove as much of the solution as possible using a gel-loading pipette tip to prevent accidental removal of gel pieces.
Dehydrate the gel pieces by adding 1 mL of 100% acetonitrile and incubate at room temperature with occasional vortexing until gel pieces turn white.
Replace acetonitrile every hour until fully dehydrated, ensuring complete removal of any residual blue stain.
Add a sufficient amount of 10 mM DTT in 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate to cover the gel pieces.
Incubate at 56°C for 1 hour.
Cool samples to room temperature (RT).
Replace the DTT solution with roughly the same volume of 55 mM iodoacetamide in 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate.
Incubate at RT for 45 minutes in the dark with occasional vortexing.
Remove the iodoacetamide solution after incubation.
Wash gel pieces with approximately 100 μL of 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate for 10 minutes while vortexing.
Dehydrate gel pieces with approximately 100 μL of 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate in 50% acetonitrile.
Remove the dehydration solution and dry the gel pieces in a vacuum centrifuge for 20 minutes.
Add 0.5 μg of mass spectrometry-grade trypsin in 5 mM ammonium bicarbonate containing 5% acetonitrile to the gel pieces.
Incubate on ice for 30 minutes to allow the gel pieces to become fully saturated with trypsin solution.
Transfer samples to a 37°C incubator for overnight digestion.
Extract digested peptides by adding enough 5% formic acid in acetonitrile to fully cover the gel pieces.
Incubate at 37°C for 15 minutes with constant agitation.
Transfer the supernatant using a gel-loading pipette tip to a new 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Concentrate the sample using a centrifugal vacuum concentrator on medium heat until 20 μL is remaining.
Repeat extraction steps by adding enough 5% formic acid in acetonitrile, incubating at 37°C for 15 minutes with constant agitation, and transferring the supernatant twice more.
After each round of extraction, concentrate the sample to approximately 20 μL using a centrifugal vacuum concentrator on medium heat.
Identify high confidence LD proteomes using mass spectrometry.
Analyze tryptic peptides using liquid chromatography coupled tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS).
Use MaxQuant software to identify peptide identities and intensities for label-free quantification.
Perform comparative analysis with controls to remove contaminant proteins.
Export the protein groups file from MaxQuant.
Open the exported protein groups file.
Use the intensity-based absolute quantification (iBAQ) value for label-free quantification.
Calculate PLIN2-APEX2N by subtracting the iBAQ intensity of cyto-APEX2 from that of PLIN2-APEX2, averaged from two biological replicates.
Calculate ATGL∗-APEX2N similarly to PLIN2-APEX2N but for ATGL∗-APEX2.
Normalize values to control for labeling of cytosolic proteins or non-specific binding to beads.
